questions.q: Why does working from the bottom of the stack up usually narrow problems faster than starting with application logs?
options: Application logs are never useful
A layer below the application (network, DNS, port) can cause an error the app logs never mention
It's required by every monitoring tool
Bottom-up checks don't require any tools
questions.explain: Lower-layer problems like routing, DNS, or a closed port can cause application-level symptoms without appearing in application logs at all.

questions.q: What is the suggested order of checks in this methodology?
options: Application, transport, DNS, reachability
Reachability, DNS, transport, application
DNS, application, reachability, transport
Transport, application, DNS, reachability
questions.explain: The methodology works bottom-up: confirm basic reachability, then DNS, then the transport/port layer, and only then the application itself.

questions.q: What does "isolating a variable" mean in troubleshooting?
options: Fixing every possible cause simultaneously
Changing or removing one factor at a time to see what the problem follows
Only checking the application logs
Ignoring user reports entirely
questions.explain: Isolating a variable means testing one factor — location, browser, account, etc. — at a time to see whether the problem tracks with it.

questions.q: What makes a hypothesis useful in troubleshooting?
options: It's vague enough to cover many possible causes
It's specific and testable, pointing to an obvious next check
It doesn't need to be tested
It should always blame the network first
questions.explain: A specific, falsifiable hypothesis — rather than a vague impression — points directly to a concrete next test.

questions.q: Why does documenting what's already been checked matter?
options: It's required by every firewall vendor
It prevents repeated work and gives the next person a clear starting point
It replaces the need for a methodology entirely
It only matters for DNS-related issues
questions.explain: A record of what was already checked and what it showed avoids duplicated effort and helps whoever picks up the issue next.
